title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
These are addenda ('rabiots') to the preceding exposé on Barsotti–Tate (BT) groups and Dieudonné crystals. The material is close to the Montréal 1970 lectures and the Nice ICM 1970 talk.

(a) Filtration over a perfect base.
- Let S = Spec A with A a perfect F_p-algebra, and let M be a Dieudonné (F-V-)crystal, i.e. a finite locally free W(A)-module with F and V. Put M_0 = M/pM.
- The Hodge filtration Fil^1 ⊂ M_0 is characterised by Fil^1^{(p)} = Ker(F_M) = Im(V_M) on M_0.
- Because Frobenius on A is bijective, Frobenius pullback is an equivalence. So Fil^1 is recovered uniquely from its Frobenius twist.
- Hence every Dieudonné crystal is 'admissible': it carries a unique compatible filtration. This is the familiar fact that over perfect rings Dieudonné modules alone determine BT groups, with no extra Hodge datum needed.

(b) Isogeny categories.
- IsoBT(S) has the same objects as BT(S), with Hom(G,H)⊗_{Z_p}Q_p = Hom⊗_Z Q.
- Grothendieck flags that this naive localisation does not give a stack and should be reconsidered. The modern fix is quasi-isogenies as a sheaf.
- Similarly he defines Dieudonné isocrystals and gets a functor IsoBT(S) → Iso-F-V-cris(S), for p locally nilpotent on S.
- Proposition (proof deferred): for a nilpotent immersion S → S' with ideal J (killed by a power of p / nilpotent), restriction IsoBT(S') → IsoBT(S) is an equivalence of categories.
  - Full faithfulness is rigidity of quasi-isogenies: if J^{N+1}=0 and p^n kills J, then p^{nN} times any homomorphism lifts.
  - Essential surjectivity is (local) unobstructedness of deformations of BT groups.
- From this he deduces 'VII 10.8.2 of my Pisa notes', with a marginal note to work out the mixed-characteristic DVR case.

Problem 4.
- Describe the essential image of the functor from (iso)BT groups to filtered (iso)crystals over a p-adically complete noetherian A.
- Is there a valuative criterion for membership?
- For a mixed-characteristic DVR, is the essential image a Zariski open subset of the Grassmannian of filtrations? The sentence is cut off at 'grassma-'.
- This is exactly the period-domain / admissibility question later answered by Fontaine's weak admissibility, Rapoport–Zink period domains, Colmez–Fontaine, Breuil and Kisin.
errors: 'J annulé par une puissance de J' (as typed) is presumably a slip for 'annulé par une puissance de p' or simply 'J nilpotent'.

Full equivalence on a general base is problematic since the naive isogeny category is not a stack. Essential surjectivity needs lifting of BT groups, which is guaranteed locally (affine) but globally only up to the stack issue Grothendieck himself flags.

Implicit answer to Problem 4 is negative in general: the weakly admissible (= admissible, Colmez–Fontaine) locus is not Zariski open. Drinfeld's half-plane P^1 \ P^1(Q_p) is an example. It is open only in the rigid/adic sense.

missed.claim: Grothendieck states, c. 1970, the equivalence of isogeny categories of BT groups under nilpotent thickening. This is the statement now attributed to Drinfeld as quasi-isogeny rigidity.
missed.quote: Soit S → S' une immersion nilpotente d'Idéal J ... alors le foncteur restriction IsoBT(S') → IsoBT(S) est une équivalence de catégories.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Possible priority note for a foundational tool of Rapoport–Zink spaces, though it may already appear in the Montréal/Pisa notes.

missed.claim: He explicitly asks whether, for a mixed-characteristic DVR, the essential image is Zariski open in the Grassmannian of filtrations, and for a valuative criterion. This anticipates the period-domain question; the answer was later found to be no (rigid-open only).

deep.surprise_reason: A draft of known problem lists (Nice ICM / Montréal). The rigidity statement predating Drinfeld and the explicit Zariski-openness question are mildly interesting historically, but both threads were fully developed later.
transcription_corrections: The inserted 'un anneau parfait' sits above 'le cas d'une base de car. p', giving 'dans le cas d'une base de car. p, un anneau parfait'.
In 'annulé par une puissance de J', the final J appears in the typescript but is likely a typo for p.
The handwritten margin note reads roughly '(Expliciter le cas d'un anneau [de valuation struck] discret d'inégales car.)'.
